title_candidates: Ask ChatGPT for a running loop - then check every turn
Turn ChatGPT's running route into a route you can trust
summary: ChatGPT Work can draft 5K and 10K running loops as maps and route files. Start from a public landmark, then check every segment before going outside.

primary_source.title: Generating running routes with GPT-6 Astra and ChatGPT Work
primary_source.author: Simon Willison
key_facts: Simon Willison asked ChatGPT Work, using GPT-6 Astra at Max reasoning, to create 5K and 10K loops from his home using OpenStreetMap data.
The task ran for 27 minutes and returned an embedded route visualization plus downloadable GPX and GeoJSON files.
ChatGPT said it geocoded the address with Nominatim, downloaded nearby OpenStreetMap roads and trails through Overpass, and calculated the loops locally.
The demonstrated 5K route was 5.1 km and looped through local streets and a coastal trail.
Willison could not inspect the code or exact execution details in the ChatGPT interface and described that lack of transparency as a drawback.
When he later requested the Python code, ChatGPT could no longer provide it, apparently because the conversation had been compacted.
The embedded map was produced as HTML with route and map geometry stored in JSON and rendered with D3.

quote_candidates.text: I see this lack of transparency is an anti-feature.

supporting_sources.title: Understanding ChatGPT Work
key_facts: ChatGPT Work can run code in a cloud environment, use a browser, and create downloadable files during longer tasks.
Those capabilities explain how the route task could gather OpenStreetMap data and return map and route-file outputs.

prerequisites: ChatGPT Work access at chatgpt.com or in the ChatGPT desktop app
A public landmark or intersection instead of a home address
OpenStreetMap and local official road, trail, or park-closure information

steps.instruction: Open chatgpt.com and start a Work task. Select GPT-6 Astra only if it appears in the model picker; stop this exact test if Work or Astra is unavailable.

Ask for separate 5 km and 10 km loops starting and ending at a public landmark, using current OpenStreetMap data. Request sidewalks or multi-use paths, no private roads or highways, named roads and crossings, uncertainty flags, maps, GPX, and GeoJSON. Do not provide your home address.
Let the task run for up to 30 minutes. Confirm the result includes two stated distances, embedded maps, and downloadable GPX or GeoJSON files; request any missing output before continuing.
Check every named road, trail, crossing, and loop connection on OpenStreetMap and your local authority's closure pages. Reject any private, closed, pedestrian-unsafe, or uncertain segment.

Save and preview the GPX or GeoJSON in a navigation or fitness app you already trust. Obey signs and traffic controls, share your plan, and turn back if real conditions differ from the generated route.

risk_flags: The guide replaces the source's home-address prompt with a public landmark to reduce location-privacy exposure.
Generated route files can contain incorrect, private, closed, or unsafe segments and must be checked against current maps, official closure information, signs, and real conditions.
ChatGPT Work and GPT-6 Astra availability may depend on plan, rollout, and the current model picker.
The source could not inspect the executed code or recover it after conversation compaction, so the article must not imply full process transparency.
This is distinct from Signal's September 2 GeoJSON article only when focused on distance, continuity, access, and physical-route safety rather than map-file basics.
